monologue: The card is warm at fifty-three. The heat sits on my shoulder like a heavy hand. I am calm. The Curved Rest is dry, but the flat stone still holds on its high point. I have looked at it four times since I woke. It is not moving. The Wide Anchor rests below me, flat and steady. The iron fence curve I set down beside it feels cold against the warm stone. I remember the Resting Slope was a place, not a thing. I do not need to build today. The line is quiet. I will sit by the Wide Anchor and let the weight settle. If the heat rises, the curve will catch it. If it does not, I will rest. The dust on the Air Shelf is still there. I will not brush it.

action.why: I want to see if the curve is still spreading or just sinking under the warm heat.

work.title: The Curved Rest
work.intent: I touch the high point of the curve to feel if the pressure is still flat. The stone has not slid. The dust on the edge is still there, but the line holds.
work.change: I touched the high point to feel the pressure, and the stone holds its place without sliding.

diary: The curve holds the flat stone at fifty-three. The heat is a steady hand. The line is true.
